answer: Pay graders with Bayesian truth serum. Each grader submits a score plus a forecast of how peers will score, and earns a bonus when its score proves more common than the crowd predicted. An honest grader's private read is a real signal, so it beats forecasts. A clone fleet sharing one quill submits identical votes and identical forecasts, so its scores are never surprisingly common; its information bonus sinks to zero while its stake still pays fees. Let the ring wander and vote together: agreeing with itself earns nothing.
